_doc: The one machine price table of yeto (yeto.cost.prices). Every row has a grade: billing (a price list a bill follows: billing, budget gates, breakers and offer pricing use it) or illustrative (an example value for estimates only: the dashboard shows it marked as an estimate; to everything that gates money it is no price). Every row: one node of `gpus` GPUs of `gpu` at `provider`, its whole-node price `usd_h` (USD per hour), where it came from (`source`) and when it was read (`as_of`). `spot` (true / false) and `region` narrow a row; a row without them matches any. A node of n GPUs is priced n / gpus x usd_h. `native` keeps a provider's own unit next to the USD price (National Compute bills in ucr). Billing, the run and pool budgets, the dashboard and the dry-runs read this table; a run config or a price file still overrides it.

rows.note: lists at 0.001972 USD/s (7.10 USD/h); kept at 8.5 so a region-pinned 2x8 B300 trainer (~136 USD/h) does not overrun its budget before the billing report catches up

services._doc: Machines priced by what they serve, not by their GPUs: per service, one row per provider the service runs on, each a whole-machine USD per hour with its grade, source and date. `syncer`: the machine a fleet's syncer runs on, billed when the run config sets no syncer.usd_per_h: the controller head VM it shares with the fleet controller (--controller head, the default) or its own syncer VM (--controller local); either is one on-demand sky VM on the --syncer-region cloud with cpus 8+ and --syncer-memory.

syncer.source: AWS EC2 on-demand Linux price list: m6i.2xlarge (8 vCPU, 32 GiB) in us-east-1 / us-west-2
syncer.note: the cheapest instance sky picks for the head / syncer VM's default resources (cpus 8+, --syncer-memory 32 GiB); a larger --syncer-memory orders a larger machine: set syncer.usd_per_h

syncer.source: Modal billing report of a two-island fleet run: the syncer's Modal CPU container (8 cores, 96 GiB) ~2.4 USD/h
syncer.note: measured on the bill; the estimate from CPU and memory list prices (1.32 USD/h) undercounted it

modal.source: https://modal.com/pricing (0.0000131 USD per physical core-second, 0.00000222 USD per GiB-second, network egress 0.04 USD per GiB); CPU and memory bill on max(request, usage), an ephemeral disk request bills as memory at 20:1 (modal.com/docs/guide/resources)
modal.note: a Modal app's estimate is its GPU row plus the cores and memory its functions request, plus the bytes its trainer's tape says it sent out of Modal (releases to a store outside Modal, fragments to a syncer) at egress_gib; checked against the Modal billing report's per-resource rows of 1xL40S verl trainer apps (8 cores, 64 GiB): the CPU and memory lines match to the cent and the egress line matches the published bytes. egress_gib ignores the plan's included egress (1 / 10 / 100 TiB a month): high, never low
